root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Reduce the product to a convolution of radix digits evaluated by approximate Fourier transforms over a polynomial ring, make the transform's address movement and arithmetic cheaper with two new tape procedures, then show the result is exact and add up the cost.

motivation.text: Scanning the data once per transform level already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so a power saving needs savings in both address movement and arithmetic, one tape procedure for each.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.
